title: Reduction of curve cohomology comparison to connected smooth curves
statement: For algebraically closed fields k subset K, a quasi-compact separated smooth curve f:C -> Spec k of relative dimension one, and natural numbers n and q, suppose the canonical cohomology pullback with constant Z/n coefficients is bijective in degree q for every connected smooth curve over k. Then it is bijective in degree q for C. The empty curve and n=0 or n=1 are included; no invertibility is needed for this component assembly.

source.place: First step: reduction by finite clopen connected components

proof.text: Finite type over the field makes C Noetherian, smoothness makes C regular, and its connected components are finitely many integral clopen smooth connected curves of dimension one. Base change preserves the clopen decomposition and connectedness over the algebraically closed base.

Use the canonical finite-coproduct cohomology product isomorphisms on C and its base change. Naturality of cohomology pullback identifies the map with the product of the component maps. Supply the hypothesis h for each component, take the product of these bijections and conjugate by the product isomorphisms. An empty product gives the empty-curve case.

theorem bijective_curve_cohomologyMap_of_connected
    {k K : Type u} [Field k] [Field K] [IsAlgClosed k] [IsAlgClosed K] [Algebra k K]
    {C : Scheme.{u}} (f : C ⟶ Spec (.of k))
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 f] [IsSeparated f] [QuasiCompact f]
    (n q : ℕ)
    (h : ∀ {D : Scheme.{u}} (g : D ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [IsConnectedCurve g] [Smooth g],
      Function.Bijective (Etale.cohomologyMap
        (pullback.fst g (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))))
        (D.constantZMod n) q)) :
    Function.Bijective (Etale.cohomologyMap
      (pullback.fst f (Spec.map (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap k K))))
      (C.constantZMod n) q)
